title: ATOMROGUE - Early alpha build of my JS roguelike
author: heisenbergpl
selftext:
Hey r/roguelikedev community!

After **2 days of intensive prototyping**, I have an early alpha build of my roguelike: **ATOMROGUE**.

**Quick dev note:** 

The core idea, architecture, and 100% of the code quality is mine - I'm a classical developer who hand-crafts everything. But I ran an experiment: I wanted to see what Claude Code could produce in a tight "vibe" session. The result? A fully playable roguelike built in \~48 hours, with me guiding, reviewing, and hand-correcting every piece.

       ╔═══════════════════════════════════╗
       ║         ATOMROGUE ALPHA           ║
       ║  "Escape the nuclear facility"    ║
       ╚═══════════════════════════════════╝

**Tech stack pure and simple:**

* Vanilla JavaScript (no frameworks, no engines)
* Custom ECS-based game engine (\~2000 lines so far)
* Procedural dungeon generator with rooms & corridors
* Turn-based tactical combat with 10+ weapon types
* Real-time terminal rendering in browser

**Biggest challenge:** Making text-based UI feel responsive. Also... the biggest challenge in the vibe is progressing the game step by step, adding new features while keeping everything that already worked functioning properly. CC can break something it just created correctly. Then it breaks itself again while doing something else. This can be mega frustrating because de facto I sometimes spent more time guiding it to fix things than creating new, more complex features from scratch.

**Current status:** Early alpha build - playable, fun, but rough around the edges. I'm looking for feedback on gameplay balance, UI clarity, and that elusive "fun factor" before I polish it further.

**Play now (desktop & mobile):** [https://atomrogue.xce.pl/](https://atomrogue.xce.pl/)

**Questions?** Ask me anything about implementation, design decisions, or the nuclear-themed nightmare that is my local testing environment.

comments.author: nefD
comments.body: Your link doesn't work. What sort of pathfinding algorithm did you use for the enemies?

replies.author: heisenbergpl
replies.body:
https://preview.redd.it/17cih581x5sg1.png?width=999&format=png&auto=webp&s=7534825d9fcf4af3508b55cd83e10e6ac6f28d2f

Hmm, strange - the link seems to work fine. I tested it in another browser and it's OK.

BFS (flood fill) is used for map calculations, while enemy movement uses simplified greedy movement with deterministic randomness, not a full pathfinding algorithm like A\*.

replies.author: nefD
replies.body: Neat! Are you going to implement any kind of light blocking or does the character always have vision around them regardless of obstacles? As a tip from a grizzled roguelike dev, look into recursive shadow casting; it's relatively fast and accurate enough for a grid.

replies.author: heisenbergpl
replies.body:
Cool! Shadow casting is definitely on my radar for the next version. Right now I'm wrestling with Claude Code to implement radioactive zones where the player accumulates RAD points that slowly kill them (unless they find an antidote).

After that I'll tackle shadowcasting properly. Overall, vibe-coding with Claude is super fast for prototyping, but yeah - it frustratingly breaks stuff that was already working along the way! 😄

replies.author: nefD
replies.body: I'm in a similar situation- veteran developer kicking the tires on vibe coding to see what it's capable of and where it falls apart. I've had pretty good luck with Claude Code when we collaborate on both a design document and a roadmap split into small, well defined phases. Anyway, looking forward to more updates on the project!

comments.author: HealthyWest6482
comments.body:
This is kinda something I've been trying to push into my project.  I'm not sure if it's something you'd want to commit to - but the tiles/walls are all procedural using Pixi JS. Runs pretty smoothly too with no CSS/DOM overhead so you can do pixi effects (lighting, distortion, hit freeze, time dilation, bloom/rotate/scale) for cool immersion stuff.

comments.author: heisenbergpl
comments.body:
Hey everyone, quick update on my roguelike browser game **ATOMROGUE**!

From its very first public version - a total experimental mess dropped just a few days ago. I've iterated fast using some LLM magic in Claude Code and Codex. This let me roll out several new builds super quickly.

# Now on v0.7 - What's New

* Fresh monsters and items to shake up gameplay.
* Proper **shadow casting** for that atmospheric lighting.
* Revamped level generation for more variety.
* Fully responsive display that adapts to mobile devices - tested smooth on emulator and my Samsung S23. iPhone should work too, but no guarantees without testing!

Load/autosave games and a Hall of Fame are in place. Jump in, test it out, climb the leaderboard!

Play here: [https://atomrogue.xce.pl/](https://atomrogue.xce.pl/)

Feedback welcome - let's make it epic!

comments.author: heisenbergpl
comments.body:
Hey everyone,

So, guess what happened? I just logged back into the server after the weekend to see what had been going on in ATOM Rogue. And you know what? The mine has a few more corpses now. That means a bunch of you actually played the game while I was away. That’s pretty cool - thanks for that!

It actually got me excited to share something I never really talked about before. In the game there’s a cemetery. No joke. When a player dies, the game saves that information: the level they were on, and what they had in their inventory. Later, other players who come to those levels can find the remains of a previous player and take some of their gear.

To make this feel more real, I added a little page called “Graveyard.” There you can see a list of the latest deaths (kind of creepy), and an indicator if there are any leftover items still waiting to be picked up. That should help all the thieves and rogues creeping around the mine in search of loot.

I also added a small popup with the basic controls and movement instructions for players who are entering the game for the first time.

If you feel like trying it out, go ahead and jump in. Happy looting!
